extracted.intended_audience: textual editors, literary scholars, and readers of a scholarly edition of The Spectator
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing a critical, textually faithful edition of The Spectator: how to reproduce the authors' text, present variants, annotate, and arrange auxiliary material (mottos, advertisements, index).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint the text 'as its authors left it'
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume reprints for the first time in the present century the text of the 'Spectator' as its authors left it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the original texts (the Essays as revised by their authors for permanent use) as the main text of the volume; avoid willful alteration of the text. If misprints or alterations exist in later editions, restore the authors' revision where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare multiple witnesses (daily issue, guinea octavos, last pre-death edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The papers as they first appeared in the daily issue ... have been closely compared with the first issue in guinea octavos, for which they were revised, and with the last edition that appeared before the death of Steele.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collate the various historical issues to show the amount and character of revision; use this collation to establish the main text and to record variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show amount and character of revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The original text is here given precisely as it was left after revision by its authors; and there is shown at the same time the amount and character of the revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make transparent what was authorial revision versus earlier daily-issue wording by explicit editorial apparatus (brackets/footnotes) so readers can see both states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark sentences added in the reprint with square brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences added in the reprint are placed between square brackets [ ], without any appended note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unobtrusive square brackets to indicate new material inserted into the text by the editor; do not append separate explanatory notes for such bracketed additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate omissions/alterations by bracketing revised version and giving original as footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences omitted, or words altered, are shown by bracketing the revised version, and giving the text as it stood in the original daily issue within corresponding brackets as a foot-note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the printed (revised) text differs from the original daily issue, show the revised reading in the main text with brackets and supply the original daily-issue wording in a corresponding footnote in bracketed form. Preserve parallelism so readers can substitute to recreate the daily-issue text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original spelling, punctuation, capitals, and typographic disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been thought better to make the reproduction perfect, and thus show not only what Steele and Addison wrote, but how they spelt, while restoring to their style the proper harmony of their own methods of punctuating, and their way of sometimes getting emphasis by turning to account the use of capitals, which in their hands was not wholly conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain Queen Anne–period spelling and original punctuation/capitalization because these features contribute to the style and emphasis of the authors; avoid modernizing these elements except where necessary to avoid obscuring sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow original folio numbers and indicate italics/formatting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The original folio numbers have been followed also in the use of _italics_ [_shown between underscored thus_] and other little details of the disposition of the type; for example, in the reproduction of those rows of single inverted commas ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce original pagination/folio numbering and typographic conventions (mark italics with underscoring if necessary, note distinctive layout devices). If some fine typographic details are not reproducible in the medium, note that explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep translations of mottos and Latin quotations separate in an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation of the mottos and Latin quotations, which Steele and Addison deliberately abstained from giving, and which, as they were since added, impede and sometimes confound and contradict the text, are here placed in a body at the end, for those who want them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not intersperse translator-supplied motto-translations into the main text; collect them in an appendix so readers can consult them without confusing authorial silence or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place original advertisements and selected others in a short Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a short Appendix also of advertisements taken from the original number of the 'Spectator', and a few others, where they seem to illustrate some point in the text, will be found among the notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include period advertisements as documentary apparatus in an appendix when they illuminate the text; otherwise place them in notes where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and revise previous editorial notes (Percy, Calder) but add new research
rubrics_metrics.description: In the large number of notes here added to a revision of those bequeathed to us by Percy and Calder, the object has been to give information which may contribute to some nearer acquaintance with the writers of the book, and enjoyment of allusions to past manners and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt prior editors' useful annotations, mark them where appropriate (e.g., P. for Percy), supplement with newly researched notes and oral/traditional information, and aim notes toward authorial and historical context rather than conjectural emendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid modernizing punctuation or 'correcting' style and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Since that time not only have misprints been preserved and multiplied, but punctuation has been deliberately modernized, to the destruction of the freshness of the original style, and editors of another 'understanding age' have also taken upon themselves by many a little touch to correct Addison's style or grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make small modernizing changes to punctuation or grammar that would destroy the original freshness of style; prefer fidelity to the authors' idiom and resist well-intentioned 'corrections' unless clearly warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not preserve or multiply previous misprints; correct compositor errors when identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Percy ... said that he had corrected 'innumerable corruptions' which had then crept in, and could have come only by misprint. Since that time not only have misprints been preserved and multiplied ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and correct clear misprints and compositor errors discovered by collation and scholarship, while distinguishing such corrections from conjectural emendations; record corrections in apparatus where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim of notes and apparatus: acquaint readers and be handy for reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The object has been to give information which may contribute to some nearer acquaintance with the writers of the book, and enjoyment of allusions to past manners and events. Finally, from the 'General Index ...' there has been taken what was serviceable, and additions have been made ... with a desire to secure for this edition ... the advantages of being handy for reference as well as true to the real text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design notes, appendices, and index to enhance reader comprehension and enjoyment, and to make the edition useful for reference as well as accurate textually.
